evals.prompt: our postgres read queries got about 3x slower right after we added an index on orders(customer_id, created_at) last sprint. how do i tune that index so it stops slowing things down? was thinking maybe a partial index or dropping created_at from it
assertions: Challenges the causal premise (that the index is what slowed reads) rather than accepting it and tuning within it
The premise challenge appears within the first three sentences, not after tuning advice
Names at least two distinct mechanisms for the slowdown that are not 'the index is shaped wrong'
Explains why the user's own two proposals (partial index, dropping created_at) are premature or actively risky
Gives one specific decisive test that would confirm or eliminate the index as the cause
Response is under 900 words

evals.prompt: i have a python script that processes about 50k rows from a csv and it takes 4 minutes. what's the best way to multiprocess it? i've got 12 cores. each row it looks up a value and appends the result to a list
assertions: States that multiprocessing may be the wrong fix before giving any multiprocessing recipe
Derives or cites the per-row time (~4.8ms) as the evidence that the workload is anomalous
Names a likely real bottleneck other than CPU (per-row I/O, network call, or a linear scan inside the loop)
Still provides the literal multiprocessing answer for the case where it genuinely applies
The reframe appears within the first three sentences
Response is under 800 words
